items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: That — I never heard them say anything about rock & roll, but when bop came in — Dizzy Gillespie, Charlie Parker, that was a different world from the world they played.

ctx.x: Yeah. Did you ever hear those fellas complain or comment about transition from swing to rock & roll?

It was more, they talked and it brings to mind when you say that, it wasn’t so much swing, the big bands, to rock & roll, it was swing music, the war, the Glenn Miller Army Air Force Band, which was like the hand picked — the best of every big band Glenn Miller got. But when the war was over nobody could afford the big bands hardly anymore. What they talked more about was when bop came in. That — I never heard them say anything about rock & roll, but when bop came in — Dizzy Gillespie, Charlie Parker, that was a…

That’s true. I never thought of it that way, from an employment standpoint. I mean you knew the band shrunk and, but yeah, especially the saxophone players, a lot of them found work in the rock & roll.
